text:
maria: Folks, seeing a ~45% throughput drop on cluster-prod-gpu-7 and a bunch of worker restarts after the 03:10 deploy. Root process OOMs and then k8s kills the pod. logs attached below. anyone oncall?

sre-bot: [ALERT] GPU_OOM spike on host gpu-7 (count=12, window=5m). Affected service: inference-runtime.

josh: I'm looking. The recent kernel selection change (coalescer heuristic) landed in the 03:06 rollout — @maria did you pin a version?

maria: Not pinned, default rollout. Here's a tail of the worker log:
```
2026-03-18T03:14:12Z runtime[pid=3421]: Alloc failed: cudaMalloc returned OUT_OF_MEMORY on size=2147483648
2026-03-18T03:14:12Z runtime[pid=3421]: Eviction loop: kv_cache evicted 1024 entries in 3s
2026-03-18T03:14:13Z k8s: Pod terminated: OOMKilled
```

remy: I grabbed a perf snapshot from the same host before it flaked. The flamegraph shows a big spike in small-allocation churn in the allocator when the coalescer is enabled. Also batch size distribution moved from median=8 to many 1-3 sized micro-batches. That increases slab fragmentation.

remy: quick summary stats: p50 latency +12ms, p95 +48ms, token throughput -46%. KV-cache hit_rate dropped from 87% -> 61% and eviction rate spiked.

ingrid: Looks like a noisy tenant opened many concurrent 1-request streams (health-checks + debug clients) which breaks batching heuristics. Combined with coalescer switching kernels for small seq-len, we end up allocating many tiny buffers and fragment the GPU heap.

josh: Yup — the new kernel routing tries to pick a narrow-kernel path for sequences < 32, but it doesn't coalesce multiple small batches into a single bigger run if they hit slightly different timing windows. The allocator ends up with many live small slabs.

ryan: Short-term mitigation: set runtime flag `--disable-coalescer` on the nodepool, and increase `max_batch_delay_ms` from 5 -> 12 for the hotspot pool to encourage batching. Also throttle the noisy tenant at the routing layer.

maria: Can we hotpatch a rollback? If we disable the coalescer quickly that might stop the fragmentation and OOMs.

josh: I can open a rollback PR for the kernel heuristic. But we can also flip the flag at runtime to avoid a full redeploy. I'm applying the flag to prod-gpu-7 now.

remy: Pushed a live profile after flipping flag. Eviction rate visibly drops, KV-cache hit climbs back to ~80% after ~90s. Throughput beginning to recover.

ingrid: Note: this is a combo failure mode — noisy-tenant + coalescer + small-batch-heavy workload. Longer term we should: (1) make kernel selection idempotent across micro-batches, (2) improve coalescing window to merge nearby micro-batches, (3) add a slab-coalescer to the allocator to avoid fragmentation.

ryan: I'll spawn a ticket for allocator slab-coalescing + regression test that simulates many 1-3 sized concurrent requests. Also suggest adding a tenant-level backpressure knob.

maria: Thanks. Observability note: add a dashboard panel for small-batch count ratio and per-tenant micro-batch rate so we get alerted earlier.

deploy-bot: Rollback plan scheduled: revert kernel-heuristic (sha: abc123) to canary at 03:28, full roll back to follow if canary stable.

maria: Great. I'll monitor. :thumbsup:

josh: Postmortem action items assigned. Will follow up with a short writeup once we confirm stability.

remy: attaching perf links: https://perf.redwood/internal/trace/1934567890 and flamegraph snapshot id=fg-20260318-0316

maria: Last check (03:29): throughput back to ~95% of baseline and no new OOM kills on gpu-7. Closing interim incident after we validate 15m of stability.

ingrid: filing long-term design RFC for allocator/coalescer changes.

maria: Thanks everyone, great triage.
